response: Cleaning a telescope mirror is a meticulous task that requires attention to detail. First, I carefully removed the dust and debris that had accumulated over the weeks. The mirror's surface was rough, and I used a soft cloth to gently wipe it down. Each motion was deliberate, as even the smallest particle could distort the view. I made sure to clean the hinge area thoroughly, as it's the most sensitive part of the mirror. The hinge was a bit stubborn, so I used a mild detergent and a soft brush to remove any stubborn residue. After cleaning, I checked the mirror's alignment to ensure it was clear and free of any scratches. The hinge was now smooth and clear, allowing for a clearer view of the night sky. I also made sure to dry the mirror completely to prevent any moisture from affecting the surface. The hinge was now in perfect condition, and the mirror was ready for use. P.P.S. Do not forget the volunteers.
